subject: Unusual sign-in to your ThisIsTea account
text:
Hello {{first_name}},

We noticed a sign-in to your ThisIsTea account from a device we don't recognise. If this wasn't you, your account and your learning progress may be at risk.

For your security, please confirm it's you and log in to your account now:
{{click_url}}

Thank you for helping us keep ThisIsTea safe.
The ThisIsTea Security Team

Manage ThisIsTea emails: {{settings_url}}
html:
Hello {{first_name}},

We noticed a sign-in to your ThisIsTea account from a device we don't recognise. If this wasn't you, your account and your learning progress may be at risk.

For your security, please confirm it's you and log in to your account now:

Log in to my account

Thank you for helping us keep ThisIsTea safe.
The ThisIsTea Security Team

Manage ThisIsTea emails

steps.who: The name said ThisIsTea, but a name in an email is easy to fake. ThisIsTea never asks you to log in through a link in an email, so this was not a normal ThisIsTea message.
steps.emotion: It used worry: the idea that a stranger was already in your account, so you would click to fix it straight away instead of checking first.
steps.ask: It wanted you to click and type your ThisIsTea password into a page that was not ours.
steps.verify: Open ThisIsTea yourself, from your bookmark or by typing the address, and check your account there. Never log in from a link in an email you didn't expect.

hints: A login link you didn't ask for is a red flag, even when the email uses the right name.
Real services let you sign in from the app or your own bookmark, not only from an email link.
